textbookText: Angle of deviation, A + = i + e  = 90 + 27.9 – 60 = 57.9o Hence, angle of emergence = 27.9o and angle of deviation = 57.9o.
1. Why don we not consider the lateral shift in prism?
2. A ray of light srikes on the glass prism at an angle of 40°. Find the angle of emergence, if
the angle of prism is 60°, and the refractive index is 1.5.
3. An equilateral prism with the refractive index of 1.45 is surrounded by water with the
refractive index of 1.33. A narrow beam of light strikes normally on one face of the prism.
Find the direction of the emergent ray.
1. Fix a white sheet on a drawing board using thumb pins. 2. Place the triangular prism resting on its triangular base and using a pencil, draw the

outline of the prism. 3. Draw a normal to one face of the prism and make an angle of incident gradually increasing from 30° and 60°. 4. Fix two pins at a distance of at least 8cm from each other on the line drawn for incident ray and mark these as P1 and P2. 5. Look for the images of the pins P1 and P2 through the other face of the prism. 6. Fix two pins at P3 and P4 so that they appear erected on the same straight line drawn for an incident ray in the next face of the prism. 7. Remove the pins and the prism. 8. Make a line joining the points P3 and P4. 9. Make necessary extensions of lines, and now mark the angle of incidence ∠i, angle of refraction ∠r, the angle of emergence ∠e, and the angle of deviation ∠ from the figure of experimental setup. 10. Repeat the experiment for more angles between 30° and 60°.
